Fact: additional_assets
What to find: Other assets released with the model (training data, training code, inference or evaluation code, checkpoints) and how to access them.
Card sections that often contain it: Model Sources, Resources, Links

Answer with status, value, quotes and section.

answer.value: Released alongside the model: a technical report PDF in the repo; an `encoding` folder with a Python reference implementation (encoding.py) and tests for prompt encoding; the deepseek-recipe Rust libraries with Python bindings (GitHub) for production prompt encoding/parsing; an `inference` folder with instructions for weight conversion and running local inference; and an `evaluation` folder with instructions for reproducing DeepSWE v1.1 results (dsh-minimal and mini-swe-agent, plus a patch for integrating dsh-minimal with Pier). No training data or training code is stated.
quotes: The [`encoding`](encoding/README.md) folder contains a self-contained Python reference implementation (`encoding.py`) with test cases for multi-turn conversations, tool calling, thinking mode, numeric reasoning effort, mid-conversation system messages, and interleaved image content.

For production use, we additionally release [deepseek-recipe](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-recipe), a set of Rust libraries with Python bindings that provides the same prompt format as a maintained, protocol-aware toolkit.
Please refer to the [`inference`](inference/README.md) folder for instructions on weight conversion and running inference locally.

The [`evaluation`](evaluation/README.md) folder contains step-by-step instructions for reproducing the DeepSWE v1.1 benchmark results, covering both the `dsh-minimal` agent and the official `mini-swe-agent`. The patch required to integrate `dsh-minimal` with [Pier](https://github.com/datacurve-ai/pier) is also included there.
